text:
US energy stocks are having a historic year:

The S&P 500 Equal Weight Energy ETF, $RSPG, is up +49.2% YTD, trading near its all-time high.

$RSPG covers US energy sector stocks in the S&P 500, with each company receiving an approximately equal weight.

The fund is now on track for its 3rd-strongest annual return since its inception in 2006.

This would also mark its 6th consecutive annual gain, its longest winning streak on record.

Only two years have had higher returns, in 2021 and 2022, at +53.7% and +52.2%, respectively.

Over the last 2 weeks, $RSPG has risen +7.5%, and if that pace continues, the fund could record its strongest annual return since inception.

Energy stocks are thriving amid the Iran War.

ticker_notes.META: Strong early Muse AI metrics: 10M users,

zh_summary: $META第三季：Muse AI在6週內獲10M+用戶（僅美加），約25%每日參與（超過Threads初期2倍），25%+購物平均購買超200美元。目標12個月內推論成本效率提升10倍，為10億+用戶建容量，更早變現，預期每美國用戶收入超現有應用家族。
en_summary: $META Q3: Muse AI 10M+ users in 6 weeks (US/Canada only), ~25% daily engagement (>2x Threads initial), 25%+ shop with avg purchase >$200. Targets 10x inference cost efficiency in 12 months, capacity for 1B+ users, earlier monetization, expects more rev per US user than Family of Apps.
text:
$META Q3 Earnings: Interesting numbers on Muse AI

— 10M+ users signed up in just six weeks, despite availability being limited to the U.S. and Canada.
— ~25% of users engage daily, more than 2x the initial engagement of Threads.
— 25%+ of users engage in shopping, with an average purchase size exceeding $200.
— Personal productivity (email, calendar management and task automation) and creativity rank as Muse’s second and third most common use cases, respectively.
— Targets a 10x+ improvement in inference cost efficiency over the next 12 months.
— Meta is building compute capacity to serve 1B+ Muse users over the next few years.
— Muse monetization will begin earlier than Meta's traditional playbook, reflecting high inference costs and significant commerce opportunities.
— Meta expects Muse to eventually generate more revenue per U.S. user than its existing Family of Apps
